Kuwait International Airport Partially Reopens at Terminal 4 with Limited Flights..

#Kuwait International Airport resumed limited operations on Sunday, April 26, 2026, following a two-month suspension of air traffic, with services restarting at Terminal 4, the hub for national carrier Kuwait Airways, Kuwait International Airport.
The reopening is being implemented under a phased plan by the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA), with current operations at around 10% capacity, handling approximately 40 flights daily compared to nearly 400 before the shutdown.
Kuwait Airways has begun operating initial flights to destinations including Cairo, Beirut, Amman, and Manila, alongside Jazeera Airways as part of the gradual restart of services.
Authorities have imposed strict entry measures at Terminal 4, allowing only ticketed passengers inside while companions are barred. A new entry system via the Satellite Building has also been introduced to manage passenger flow.
Officials said the airport will continue expanding operations gradually as safety and readiness conditions allow. #الكويت

LOOK: Firefighters put out a fire that hit a grass-covered area in Barangay Talon Dos, Las Piñas City, on Sunday afternoon, April 26.

The blaze spreads quickly due to dry vegetation and intense heat. The Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) records heat index levels under the “danger” category in parts of the country, increasing fire risks. Prolonged high temperatures this dry season leave open areas highly susceptible to ignition. Authorities urge residents to avoid open burning and remain alert against possible fires.

📷 Mark Balmores | MB
